leagues.name: Major international flat-racing meetings with Gulf state-linked sponsors
leagues.country: Global (Saudi Arabia, UAE, France, United Kingdom)
notes: Event-host shape: these 6 meetings do not fit the schema yet (no event entity, no host/title-sponsor placement), so the meetings are recorded here as the entity list and every commercial fact is recorded in unsourced and as org deals, following the UFC and Esports World Cup precedent. clubs and kits arrays are empty.

The 6 meetings: Saudi Cup meeting (13-14 Feb 2026, King Abdulaziz Racecourse, Riyadh), Dubai World Cup meeting (28 Mar 2026, Meydan Racecourse), Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe weekend (3-4 Oct 2026, ParisLongchamp), Qatar Goodwood Festival (28 Jul - 1 Aug 2026, Goodwood), Qatar Racing British Champions Day (17 Oct 2026, Ascot), Emirates Poules d'Essai French Guineas day (10 May 2026, ParisLongchamp).

Sponsorship is on race titles and meeting titles, not shirts: each race card carries its own presenting partners, which change yearly. Race names embed sponsors (Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, Neom Turf Cup, 1351 Turf Sprint, Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes).

Distinguish state bodies from private royal-family vehicles: Jockey Club of Saudi Arabia, QREC, Abu Dhabi Sports Council, Visit Qatar, Emirates and the PIF projects (Qiddiya, NEOM) are state or state-fund money; QIPCO and Qatar Racing are private companies of members of Qatar's ruling family; Godolphin is the Dubai ruler's own racing operation.
Title switches matter: QIPCO extended British Champions Day to 2028 on 22 Jun 2026, then on 4 Aug 2026 the headline sponsorship moved to its subsidiary Qatar Racing for three years.

proposedRatings.reasoning: Qiddiya City is wholly owned by PIF, the Saudi sovereign wealth fund chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and its race-presenter role at the state-organised Saudi Cup is direct Saudi state money in a flagship international event; same evidentiary base as the other rated PIF sponsors (record 345 executions in 2024, Khashoggi assessment). Serious, not severe: no armed-conflict link.

SNB's own annual report names PIF as the ultimate controlling party (37.2%), so the bank presents a race at the state-run Saudi Cup as an arm of the Saudi state; serious, matching the PIF chain rating.

Qatar Racing is the racing arm of QIPCO, a private investment company of Qatar's ruling Al Thani family (Sheikh Fahad and Sheikh Hamad Al Thani), now buying the title of Britain's richest raceday and all seven races; ruling-family money buys national prestige, so it rates serious, not severe - it is a private family company, not a Qatar state body.

Same chain as Qatar Racing: a private Qatari royal-family investment company that has funded British Champions Day since 2011 and to 2028; the rating follows the family link rather than state control.

QREC is a Qatari state body (state domain qrec.gov.qa, chairman credits the leadership) that has put Qatar's name on the Arc and 14 other French Group races since 2008 - direct state sponsorship of Europe's richest turf race; serious under the Qatar government chain.

Abu Dhabi Sports Council is an Abu Dhabi government body established by Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed and buys the naming rights to the French Guineas; same UAE government chain as the rated serious Etihad and Experience Abu Dhabi (2024 mass-trial life sentences, upheld 2025).
Already rated serious; the Goodwood presenting deal extends the same Qatari state tourism money from F1 to one of Britain's biggest race meetings, so the existing tier carries over.
Already rated serious; the $12m Dubai World Cup purse sponsorship on top of the official-airline role is more of the same Dubai-government sportswashing spend, no change.

A Swiss watchmaker in the Swatch Group (listed company, no state owner found on the pages checked); it presents races at the Saudi Cup meeting and in France, but nothing state-linked was found, so 'none' pending a deeper look at Swatch Group shareholders.
UK insurance broker that describes its business as grounded in employee ownership - no state owner; presenting partner of the Neom Turf Cup but the company itself is not state-linked.

unsourced: EVENT-HOST SHAPE - the schema has no event entity and no host/title-sponsor placement, so the six meetings and their race-by-race sponsorship facts are recorded here, following the UFC precedent. Meeting dates and purses: Saudi Cup meeting 13-14 Feb 2026, King Abdulaziz Racecourse, Riyadh - meeting purse $35.35m, $20m Saudi Cup (world's richest race), won by Forever Young (JCSA, 'Story So Far of The Saudi Cup', https://www.jcsa.sa/en/saudi-cup/saudi-cup-story-so-far/, and JCSA race report https://www.jcsa.sa/en/news/20260214_saudicup/, both opened). 2027 edition: 5-6 Feb 2027 at King Abdulaziz Racecourse (jcsa.sa/en/saudi-cup/, opened). Dubai World Cup meeting: Saturday 28 March 2026, Meydan, US$30.5m across nine races, $12m feature won by Magnitude (https://www.dubairacingclub.com/ and https://www.dubairacingclub.com/about-us/, opened). Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe weekend: 3-4 Oct 2026, ParisLongchamp, EUR 5m purse (https://billetterie.france-galop.com/en/event/qatar-prix-de-larc-de-triomphe/, opened). Qatar Goodwood Festival: 28 Jul - 1 Aug 2026, five days (day-by-day guide https://www.goodwood.com/horseracing/qatar-goodwood-festival/day-by-day-guide/ and the 2027 tickets page naming 'Qatar Goodwood Festival presented by Visit Qatar', https://www.goodwood.com/horseracing/qatar-goodwood-festival/tickets-and-packages/, both opened). Qatar Racing British Champions Day: Saturday 17 Oct 2026, Ascot, GBP 4.35m, seven races all individually sponsored by Qatar Racing (https://britishchampionsday.com/race-information/ and the 4 Aug 2026 announcement, both opened). Emirates Poules d'Essai: Sunday 10 May 2026, ParisLongchamp (https://billetterie.france-galop.com/en/event/emirates-poules-dessai/, opened).

RACE TITLES THAT EMBED SPONSORS, per organiser pages opened: Saudi Cup card (TDN entries, https://www.thoroughbreddailynews.com/black-type-analysis-can-shin-emperor-double-up-in-neom-turf-cup-2/, opened; corroborated by JCSA race reports of 14 Feb 2026): 1351 Turf Sprint presented by Qiddiya City; Riyadh Dirt Sprint presented by Saudi National Bank; Neom Turf Cup presented by Howden; Red Sea Turf Handicap presented by Longines; Saudi Derby presented by ZOOD Realty; Tuwaiq Cup presented by SHG; the $20m Saudi Cup itself carries no presenting sponsor. Longines also presented the H.H. The Amir Trophy ($2.5m) in Doha the same weekend. Dubai World Cup meeting: the UAE Derby is 'Sponsored By Atlantis The Royal Dubai' per dubairacingclub.com's DWC news page (https://www.dubairacingclub.com/dubai-world-cup/, opened); other 2026 race-by-race presenters not confirmed. Goodwood 2026 race titles (day-by-day guide, opened): Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes (29 Jul), Qatar Nassau Stakes (30 Jul), King George Qatar Stakes (31 Jul), Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup (28 Jul), Coral Golden Mile and Coral Stewards' Cup; the 2026 Markel Magnolia Cup charity race was on Thursday 30 July with Education Above All as beneficiary (https://www.goodwood.com/horseracing/qatar-goodwood-festival/magnolia-cup/, opened). Arc weekend supporting races carry Qatar titles (Qatar Prix du Cadran, Qatar Arabian Trophy, Qatar Prix de Jean-Luc Lagardere) and Cygames is a 'partner of the Qatar Prix de l'Arc a Triomphe' plus title sponsor of the Grand Prix de Paris since 2025 (France Galop ticketing and partners pages, opened).

MEETING ORGANISERS AND STATE LINKS: JCSA organises the Saudi Cup meeting (jcsa.sa footer: 'established in 1965... tasked with the organisation, development and promotion of Saudi Arabian horseracing'; history page records the King Faisal royal decree); no page found stating current royal patronage of the meeting in so many words - the 'under the patronage of King Salman' line in the target leads was not confirmed to a fetched source. Dubai Racing Club 'serves to organise and host horseracing at Meydan Racecourse', formed 1992; the first 1981 Dubai meeting was 'organised by the office of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai' (https://www.dubairacingclub.com/about-us/, opened); the page does not state Sheikh Mohammed owns or commissioned Meydan, so that claim stays unverified. The Saudi Cup and Dubai World Cup are state-organised meetings rather than conventionally sponsored events; the race purses are the sponsorable asset.

QREC GOVERNMENT STATUS: QREC operates on the Qatari state domain qrec.gov.qa (including trainers.qrec.gov.qa and land.qrec.gov.qa) and its chairman credits 'the generous support of our wise leadership', but no fetched page states outright that QREC is a government body (https://qrec.gov.qa/ and https://qrec.gov.qa/en/about-us, both opened). The reported 2023-2027 extension of the Arc sponsorship is a search-result claim only, not verified in a fetched source. France Galop's partners page (opened) is the primary source for 'since 2008... 14 other Group races' and the Qatar Arabian World Cup since 2014 (EUR 1m).

QIPCO / QATAR RACING CORPORATE DETAIL: the primary sources (both britishchampionsday.com announcements, opened) name 'Qatar Holdings and Investment Company (QIPCO)' and describe Qatar Racing as 'the global horse racing and breeding operation of the QIPCO group' chaired in practice by HH Sheikh Fahad Al Thani with QIPCO chaired by HH Sheikh Hamad Al Thani; QIPCO's own website (qipcoholding.com) did not resolve from this session (DNS failure), so no filing-level verification of QIPCO's corporate structure or shareholding was possible. QIPCO is a private royal-family company - not a Qatari state entity - and any rating text must say so.

GODOOLPHIN / SHADWELL SILKS: the target notes that jockey silks carry owners' colours (Godolphin, Qatar Racing, Shadwell) rather than sponsor branding; Godolphin is described in the leads as the Dubai ruler's racing operation, but no primary document was fetched this pass, and silks are out of scope for the kit schema. Left unverified.

AL SHAQAB GOODWOOD CUP: the Group 1 Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup opens the 2026 Qatar Goodwood Festival (goodwood.com day-by-day guide, opened). Al Shaqab is understood to be Qatar Foundation's equestrian arm, but no primary document confirming the ownership chain (Al Shaqab -> Qatar Foundation -> Qatari state) was fetched this pass, so no sponsor entry beyond a note was created.

ZOOD REALTY: presenter of the Saudi Derby at the 2026 Saudi Cup meeting (TDN, opened). zoodrealty.com resolves only to a bare 'The Block | by ZOOD' page with no company description, and zoodholding.com did not resolve; ownership, country of incorporation and any state links are unresolved.

SHG: presenter of the Tuwaiq Cup (TDN, opened). The existing sponsor note already flags that SHG's exact legal name is unconfirmed; no new evidence found this pass. The target leads noted the 1351 Turf Sprint was reportedly previously sponsored by stc - not verified to a fetched source.
